pr_title: Add protocol upload / download sensors to Deluge
pr_body:
<!--

## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->
This adds two new sensors to the Deluge integration, "Protocol upload rate" and "Protocol download rate"
This prevents the existing sensors "download" and "upload" rate from going negative, as it was subtracting the current upload or download rate by the respective protocol upload/download rate.

## Type of change
<!--
  What type of change does your PR introduce to Home Assistant?
  NOTE: Please, check only 1! box!

- [x] Breaking change (fix/feature causing existing functionality to break)
- [ ] Code quality improvements to existing code or addition of tests

## Breaking Change

The existing sensors, Upload speed and download speed will no longer go negative (as they are no longer having the protocol traffic subtracted from their value)

Two new sensors are added, protocol traffic upload speed and protocol traffic download speed

issue_context.title: Deluge integration is logging negative upload/download values
issue_context.body:
### The problem

The deluge integration seems to be logging negative values for the upload and download speed sensors. I looked at the code, and it is using `deluge_client` to make the XMLRPC calls, but that is reporting 0 , and i've not actually got it to return negative values, so maybe it is something after the data gets returned from the deluge_client library?


![2024-05-28 02_52_05](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/assets/802786/820d1c53-06c6-4c18-b1d8-c6d7b24f12b3)

![2024-05-28 02_53_09](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/assets/802786/c3fbaaa8-d194-4f6e-af9a-073d725fd55c)

```plaintext
>>> import deluge_client
>>> c = deluge_client.DelugeRPCClient("10.0.0.234", "58846", "homeassistant", "REDACTED")
>>> x.connect()
>>> c.call("core.get_session_status", ["upload_rate", "download_rate", "dht_upload_rate", "dht_download_rate"])
{b'upload_rate': 0.0, b'download_rate': 0.0, b'dht_upload_rate': 505.5, b'dht_download_rate': 216.0}
>>> c.call("core.get_session_status", ["upload_rate", "download_rate", "dht_upload_rate", "dht_download_rate"])
{b'upload_rate': 0.0, b'download_rate': 0.0, b'dht_upload_rate': 0.0, b'dht_download_rate': 0.0}
>>> c.call("core.get_session_status", ["upload_rate", "download_rate", "dht_upload_rate", "dht_download_rate"])
{b'upload_rate': 0.0, b'download_rate': 0.0, b'dht_upload_rate': 0.0, b'dht_download_rate': 0.0}
```

You are seeing negative values if the transport overhead exceeds the download/upload rate. This usually happens when nothing is actually being downloaded but you still have the overhead. Not actually a problem, just how the sensors were designed.

does it make sense to subtract the upload/download rate by the protocol traffic upload/download rate? they both happen independently of each other, i feel like the intention was to expose the protocol traffic those could be made as separate sensors? For me it doesn't make sense to have a negative value at all , as you cannot really have a negative download rate.

the client also exposes these separately as well, without subtracting:

![image](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/assets/802786/a0942d18-0074-4204-b786-a4a2f6089f60)
This was simply how the integration was made. By the time I did my work in getting in the config flow, it was already done. Pull requests are always welcome to create new sensors for transport.

i created a PR to pull out those two metrics into separate sensors:

https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/119203

review_comments: Might work to do list(DelugeGetSessionStatusKeys) when you use StrEnum instead.
see above comment, deluge-client doesn't seem to like it it if `DelugeRPCClient.call` has non primitive arguments
Make it a StrEnum, then each value is still a string and you can avoid the .value

so i looked into this, i made the change but deluge-client doesn't like this

it seems that Deluge's XMLRPC is using Bencoding (aka the binary serialization used in torrents), and it is trying to convert the arguments based on the `type()` of the object, and it blows up when it is not a primitive type that it knows how to convert

you can see the code here: https://github.com/JohnDoee/deluge-client/blob/abca22ccb300593790aad6651be583a9b06229a7/deluge_client/rencode.py#L378C1-L379C39

and here it is in the python REPL:

```plaintext
>>> class DelugeKey(enum.Enum):
...  DownloadSpeed="download_rate"
...
>>> x.call("core.get_session_status", [x.value for x in list(DelugeKey)])
{b'download_rate': 947.5}
>>> x.call("core.get_session_status", list(DelugeKey))
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "<stdin>", line 1, in <module>
  File "C:\Users\auror\AppData\Roaming\Python\Python312\site-packages\deluge_client\client.py", line 265, in call
    self._send_call(self.deluge_version, self.deluge_protocol_version, method, *args, **kwargs)
  File "C:\Users\auror\AppData\Roaming\Python\Python312\site-packages\deluge_client\client.py", line 165, in _send_call
    req = zlib.compress(dumps(req))
                        ^^^^^^^^^^
  File "C:\Users\auror\AppData\Roaming\Python\Python312\site-packages\deluge_client\rencode.py", line 429, in dumps
    encode_func[type(x)](x, r)
  File "C:\Users\auror\AppData\Roaming\Python\Python312\site-packages\deluge_client\rencode.py", line 379, in encode_list
    encode_func[type(i)](i, r)
  File "C:\Users\auror\AppData\Roaming\Python\Python312\site-packages\deluge_client\rencode.py", line 379, in encode_list
    encode_func[type(i)](i, r)
  File "C:\Users\auror\AppData\Roaming\Python\Python312\site-packages\deluge_client\rencode.py", line 379, in encode_list
    encode_func[type(i)](i, r)
  [Previous line repeated 1 more time]
KeyError: <enum 'DelugeKey'>
>>>
```
This looks to be a breaking change. Previously it was the non dht data rate. Now the sensors report something else.

Well, before it was reporting the Upload / Download value, after it was subtracts the DHT (Protocol traffic) upload / download value (a bit confusing , as it was using index into DATA_KEYS, which is why I refactored that)

That was the inspiration for this PR, as if the up/down rate is 0 and the DHT up/down is > 0, this sensor would report negative

I'm not entirely sure on what constitutes a breaking change as this is my first PR, but if the value representing slightly different information counts , I can mark it as a breaking change
i have marked the PR as a breaking change
